chunks: He said: "O my people, have you considered that if I am upon clear proof from my Lord and He has given me mercy from Him, then who will support me against Allah if I disobey Him? You will only add to my loss."
ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Hud say about his relationship with God and his people's role in his fate?
ai.summary: In this verse from Surah Hud, Prophet Hud (AS) addresses his people with a rhetorical inquiry, asserting that if he possesses clear divine proof and mercy, no one can protect him from Allah should he disobey, rendering their support or opposition ultimately futile for his spiritual standing. Shia exegesis highlights this as a demonstration of the Prophet's absolute reliance on God (Tawakkul) and the insufficiency of worldly alliances against divine decree. The phrase 'ghayr takhsir' (other than loss) underscores that any deviation from the truth would result in spiritual deficit, reinforcing the concept of prophetic infallibility (Ismah) in conveying the message.
